title: Welcome to BlackRock Corporate site
gist: Despite a generic landing-page title, the text is a summary page for BlackRock Investment Institute's August 2026 "Income restored – but stay flexible" report: a structurally higher yield regime has lifted the average yield of its strategic portfolio to 5.6% from 2.3% five years ago and pushed over 80% of the global bond universe above 4%, while the long end's traditional ballast function has weakened. The stated driver is a supply-scarce macro regime in which the AI capex boom, energy/labor/geopolitical constraints and a shift from efficiency to resilience keep inflation persistent and competition for capital intense.

themes.theme: Income restored at the portfolio level

insights.claim: The average yield in BlackRock Investment Institute's strategic portfolio is now 5.6%, up from 2.3% five years ago, restoring income as a core source of portfolio returns.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A 330bp rise in strategic-portfolio yield means return targets can be met with far less duration or equity beta than in the 2021 regime — rebuild the income sleeve rather than reaching for capital gains.
insights.quote: In our strategic portfolio, the average yield is now 5.6%, up from 2.3% five years ago, creating richer income opportunities across fixed income markets.
insights.locator: Higher global government bond yields have restored

insights.claim: Analysis of LSEG data shows more than 80% of the global bond universe now yields above 4%, as of July 31, 2026.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Income is no longer a niche trade confined to credit or EM — the breadth means investors can source 4%+ yields with much less concentration risk, and screens should focus on relative risk-adjusted carry rather than absolute yield.
insights.quote: our analysis of LSEG data shows over 80% of the global bond universe now yields above 4%

insights.claim: The income opportunity created by higher yields is characterized as broader and more durable rather than a cyclical window that will quickly close.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Framing the yield level as durable argues against waiting for a better entry point; it implies locking in carry now rather than sitting in cash for a re-test of higher yields.

themes.theme: Structural yield reset, not a cycle

insights.claim: Developed market government bond yields have reset structurally higher from their Covid-19 pandemic lows, reflecting a new macro regime rather than a temporary cyclical overshoot.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: If the reset is structural, mean-reversion trades that assume yields return to pre-2020 levels are the wrong bet; discount rates, terminal-value assumptions and liability hedging should be rebased.
insights.locator: Developed market government bond yields have reset

insights.claim: The AI buildout is described as the fastest capital spending cycle in history, and it is landing in a world constrained by scarcity of energy, labor and geopolitical stability.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: The collision of record capex with hard real-resource constraints is the mechanism behind higher yields — watch power, grid and skilled-labor bottlenecks as the transmission channel from AI spending into rates.
insights.quote: The AI buildout, the fastest capital spending cycle in history, is unfolding in a world shaped by supply scarcity
insights.locator: Developed market government bond yields have reset

insights.claim: Supply scarcity is driving a broad shift in corporate and policy priorities from efficiency to resilience.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: An efficiency-to-resilience regime implies structurally higher input costs and capex intensity — favors owners of scarce physical capacity and penalizes margin models built on just-in-time optimization.
insights.quote: constraints on energy, labor and geopolitics are driving a shift from efficiency to resilience
insights.locator: Developed market government bond yields have reset

insights.claim: Pressure on real resources is keeping inflation more persistent while intensifying competition for finite pools of capital.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Persistent inflation plus capital scarcity means the real cost of financing stays elevated — a headwind for leveraged and capital-hungry business models and a tailwind for lenders and holders of existing high-coupon paper.
insights.quote: These pressures on real resources are keeping inflation more persistent and intensifying competition for finite pools of capital.
insights.locator: Developed market government bond yields have reset

insights.claim: Long-term government bonds have been hit hardest in the yield reset because policy rates have risen and investors now demand greater compensation for holding long-duration government debt.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: The damage is concentrated at the long end, so curve positioning matters more than aggregate duration — the article's logic favors harvesting yield away from the longest maturities.
insights.locator: Long-term government bonds have been hit hardest

insights.claim: Long-term government bond yields have been pushed to multi-year highs across the globe.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A synchronized global move in long yields limits the diversification benefit of spreading duration across countries; watch long-end auctions and term-premium measures as the key risk indicator.
insights.quote: It’s pushed long-term government bond yields to multi-year highs across the globe.
insights.locator: Long-term government bonds have been hit hardest

insights.claim: The traditional ballast role of long-term government bonds — cushioning selloffs in risk assets — has weakened.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Directly challenges the 60/40 hedging assumption: portfolios need alternative shock absorbers rather than relying on long duration to rally in an equity drawdown.
insights.quote: the traditional ballast role that long-term government bonds have played, helping cushion risk asset selloffs, has also weakened

insights.claim: Yield to maturity in bonds does not always provide the same compensation for risk, making security selection more important than headline yield.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: A screening rule: rank bonds by risk-adjusted carry rather than nominal yield, since two 5% yields can carry very different duration, credit and liquidity risk in this regime.
insights.quote: the yield to maturity in bonds does not always provide the same compensation for risk
insights.locator: This environment makes selectivity even more important

insights.claim: Abundant income opportunities are paired with an explicit call for flexibility because the risk landscape is shifting.
insights.speaker: BlackRock Investment Institute
insights.so_what: Implies dynamic rather than buy-and-hold fixed income allocation — keep the ability to rotate across curve, geography and credit quality as the regime evolves.
insights.quote: Opportunities are abundant, but navigating a shifting risk landscape requires a flexible approach.
